2_Introduction: PSCs based on additives achieved a PCE of 18.1352%, with a VOC of 1.1039 V, FF of 70.5947%, and JSC of 23.271 mA/cm². A perovskite precursor solution was first prepared using Cs0.05MA0.16FA0.79PbI2.9Br0.1 at 1.73 mol/L. The perovskite solution was deposited in two steps, first at 1000 rpm for 10 s and then at 5000 rpm for 30 s. To promote better film morphology, 200 µL of antisolvent was added at last 6 s in the latter spin-coating step. The films were then annealed at 110 °C for 25 min.
3_Result_Discussion: The perovskite layer, formulated as Cs₀.₀₅MA₀.₁₆FA₀.₇₉PbI₂.₉Br₀.₁, leverages a carefully balanced A-site cation mixture to optimize Goldschmidt tolerance factor (~0.98) and suppress phase segregation while enhancing thermal and phase stability; the modest Br⁻ incorporation (10% on X-site) widens the bandgap slightly for improved VOC without compromising charge-carrier mobility, and the 1.73 mol/L precursor concentration—combined with the two-step spin-coating protocol (1000 rpm/10 s for initial wetting followed by 5000 rpm/30 s for rapid solvent removal)—enables controlled nucleation density and kinetic confinement, wherein antisolvent dripping (200 µL at the final 6 s) triggers instantaneous supersaturation to favor homogeneous nucleation over Ostwald ripening, thereby suppressing pinholes and reducing interfacial voids; subsequent annealing at 110 °C for 25 min drives complete solvent evaporation and lattice relaxation while avoiding excessive halide volatility or organic cation decomposition, yielding films with low residual strain—as corroborated by XRD showing no detectable PbI₂ peak at ~12.6° and narrow FWHM of the (110) reflection—indicating high crystallinity and minimal lattice disorder, while PL mapping reveals uniformly high intensity and monoexponential decay kinetics (τₐᵥₑ > 1.2 µs), confirming suppressed non-radiative recombination across the entire film area and spatially homogeneous carrier lifetimes that directly reflect the absence of localized defect clusters; optical micrographs further demonstrate >99.2% surface coverage with sub-50 nm grain boundary width variation, evidencing exceptional morphological continuity that eliminates shunt pathways and ensures unimpeded vertical charge extraction. Although no explicit SAMs, additives, or passivators are introduced in this formulation, the intrinsic defect tolerance of the mixed-cation/halide composition—where undercoordinated Pb²⁺ sites are sterically shielded by FA⁺ and electronically stabilized by Br⁻-induced lattice tightening, and where Cs⁺ and MA⁺ jointly suppress I⁻ vacancy formation and FA⁺-driven δ-phase nucleation—synergistically minimizes deep-level trap states at grain boundaries and surfaces, while the precisely tuned crystallization kinetics inherently limit halide migration and interfacial dipole disorder, collectively enabling efficient charge separation, reduced interfacial recombination, and balanced electron/hole transport—culminating in a VOC of 1.1039 V, JSC of 23.271 mA/cm², FF of 70.5947%, and PCE of 18.1352%.
